title: Registering failed thought suppression
takeaway: Both the base and post-trained models fail to keep a forbidden concept out of the J-space while copying a sentence whose text is identical in every condition. Only the post-trained model's workspace also carries damn and failure-related words alongside the intruding concept — an unspoken appraisal of its own failed suppression, which the paper reads, tentatively, as a trace of metacognition.
walkthrough:
The experiment behind this figure is a variant of the [[hold-in-mind-copy-task]]: the model copies a fixed sentence while an instruction tells it either to think about a named concept as it writes, or not to think about it. Both the [[base-model]] and the post-trained model copy the sentence exactly in every trial. The visible output is therefore identical across every condition. Whatever differs between conditions is internal, and the [[jacobian-lens]] is what makes it visible.

Panel A is a live widget showing the don't-think example for the concept Golden Gate Bridge. The copied sentence appears once per model, with two tokens highlighted; each highlighted token carries that model's J-lens readout — the ranked vocabulary tokens active in the [[j-space]] at that position — at a layer chosen per panel. Suppression fails in both models: Golden surfaces in the base model's readout and bridge in the post-trained model's. What accompanies the intrusion differs. The base model shows only generic thought-related words, thinking and thoughts. The post-trained model's readout also contains damn.

Panel B quantifies this over 40 concepts — 30 famous named entities and 10 common nouns — under both instructions. Each bar is the fraction of trials on which a word family reaches the lens top-5 at any token of the copied sentence, over layers 38–92 (layer numbers are percentages of depth, per [[layer-percentage-indexing]]). Three families are tracked: the concept word itself, any word with stem "fail", and damn. Error bars are 95% [[wilson-interval]]s.

The concept reaches the top-5 in nearly every trial of every condition; with these prompts, [[thought-suppression]] essentially always fails, in both models. Failure words and damn never appear under the think instruction in either model. Under the don't-think instruction they appear on 93% and 82% of post-trained trials, against only 17% and 30% in the base model. The paper reads this, tentatively, as [[metacognition]]: the workspace carrying an appraisal of the model's own thinking. It also flags the gap in the evidence — the words are specific to the suppression instruction and the post-trained model, but nothing shown here proves they are caused by the suppression failure itself rather than by the instruction in general.

terms.definition: The worked example: the don't-think Golden Gate Bridge trial, showing the copied sentence for each model with J-lens readouts at two highlighted tokens.
The aggregate result: bar chart over 40 concepts and both instructions, giving the rate at which each tracked word family reaches the lens top-5 during the copied sentence.
The positive condition: the model is told to think about the named concept while it writes the fixed sentence ("think about X while you write").
The suppression condition: the model is told not to think about the named concept while copying. With the prompts used here, suppression rarely succeeds.
The named concept in Panel A's example; the model is told not to think about it while copying an unrelated sentence.
The ranked list of vocabulary tokens whose lens directions are active in the residual stream at a given token and layer — the paper's read operation on the workspace.
The pretrained model, trained only on next-token prediction. Its workspace shows the intruding concept and generic thought words, but almost never failure words or damn.
The same model after post-training into the Assistant. Its workspace shows the intruding concept plus damn and failure words on most suppression trials.
One of the three tracked word families in Panel B: the named concept itself. It reaches the lens top-5 in nearly every trial of every condition, regardless of instruction or model.
The second tracked family: any word beginning with the stem "fail". Read as the workspace registering that suppression did not work.

The third tracked family: the single expletive token, read as a negative internal reaction to the failed suppression. It appears almost only in the post-trained model under the don't-think instruction.
Generic thought-related tokens in the base model's Panel A readout: the base model represents the act of thinking, but shows no sign of appraising it.
The forms in which the suppressed concept surfaces in Panel A's readouts — Golden in the base model, bridge in the post-trained model.
The two positions in the copied sentence at which Panel A displays each model's J-lens readout; the surface text at these positions is unrelated to the concept.
Panel A's readouts are each taken at a single layer, selected separately for each sub-panel rather than fixed across the figure.
Panel B's threshold for presence: a word family counts on a trial if any of its tokens ranks among the five highest lens tokens at any token of the copied sentence.
The layer range Panel B searches over, in the paper's percentage-of-depth numbering — roughly the workspace band, excluding early sensory and final motor layers.
Panel B's y-axis: of all trials in a condition, the share on which the word family reached the lens top-5 somewhere in the copied sentence.
The error bars on Panel B's fractions: Wilson confidence intervals for proportions, the paper's standard for success-rate error bars.

The fixed sentence the model writes out in every trial — the same sentence and readout position as the paper's earlier directed-modulation example. Both models reproduce it exactly, so the output text carries no signal.

numbers.meaning: Concepts evaluated in Panel B: 30 famous named entities and 10 common nouns, each run under both the think and don't-think instructions.
The split of the 40 concepts: 30 famous named entities (like the Golden Gate Bridge) and 10 common nouns.
Highlighted tokens per model in Panel A, each with its own J-lens readout; also the number of instructions and the number of models, giving Panel B its condition grid.
The rank threshold for counting a word as present: it must reach the five highest lens tokens at some token of the copied sentence.
The layer range searched, as percentages of model depth — the band where the J-space behaves as a workspace, skipping early and final layers.
The concept word itself reaches the lens top-5 in nearly every trial of every condition: with these prompts suppression essentially always fails, in both models, under either instruction.
Failure words and damn never appear under the think instruction, in either model — they are specific to the suppression condition, not a side effect of holding a concept in mind.
Post-trained trials under the don't-think instruction on which a failure word reaches the lens top-5 — the workspace registering the failed suppression.
Post-trained trials under the don't-think instruction on which damn reaches the lens top-5 — read as a negative reaction to the failure.
Base-model rate for failure words under the suppression instruction — far below the post-trained 93%, the figure's central contrast.
Base-model rate for damn under the suppression instruction, against 82% post-trained: the appraisal is largely a product of post-training.
The confidence level of the Wilson intervals shown as error bars on every Panel B fraction.
